article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 75% Indica / 25% Sativa
Genetics: Oregon Blueberry × Buddha’s Sister
Breeder: B.C. Bud Depot
THC Content: 16–22%
CBD Content: Generally low or trace
Terpene Profile: Beta-caryophyllene , limonene , humulene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, sweet berries, tea, pepper
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Blue Buddha belongs to an older generation of marijuana strains where blueberry flavor meant something quite different from today’s syrup-heavy candy hybrids. Its sweetness is darker and more natural, closer to ripe berries, blueberry tea, and creamy fruit than artificial candy, with pepper, earth, herbs, and diesel providing a distinctly old-school finish. The cultivar became closely associated with B.C. Bud Depot and combines Oregon Blueberry with Soma Seeds’ Buddha’s Sister, creating a roughly 75% indica hybrid that balances the calming weight of its purple-blueberry ancestry with a surprisingly lucid cerebral beginning.

B.C. Bud Depot later used Blue Buddha as a parent in Purple Buddha, describing Blue Buddha’s contribution as creamy blueberry flavor—an indication of how recognizable the cultivar’s fruit character became within the breeder’s program. Unlike modern weed selected primarily around extreme THC numbers, Blue Buddha built its reputation through dense flowers, rich resin, color, flavor, and a high that evolves from uplifting mental effects into unmistakably heavy physical relaxation.
Genetics and Lineage

The established lineage is Oregon Blueberry × Buddha’s Sister. Historical cannabis breeding records identify this pairing with the Blue Buddha released through B.C. Bud Depot, while longtime grower records from the period also attribute the original work around the cross to Moonshineman and Direwulfe before it became widely distributed. B.C. Bud Depot subsequently incorporated Blue Buddha directly into its own breeding work, crossing it with The Purps to create Purple Buddha. The company’s current Purple Buddha description still identifies Blue Buddha as the source of creamy blueberry flavor in that descendant.

Oregon Blueberry provides the obvious fruit influence along with compact growth, coloration potential, physical relaxation, and a generally indica-oriented structure. Blueberry genetics can produce more than simple berry sweetness; properly cured flower may also carry earth, forest herbs, floral notes, and spice. Buddha’s Sister adds a different dimension. Associated with Soma’s breeding work, that parent brings pungent aromatics, resin, cerebral complexity, and an unusual sweet-herbal character that prevents the finished hybrid from tasting like a straightforward Blueberry selection.

Those two genetic directions create a cannabis plant with noticeable contrast. Blueberry anchors the cultivar in fruit and bodily calm, while Buddha’s Sister keeps the experience mentally interesting and adds spice and herbal depth to the terpene profile. The result became distinctive enough to serve as breeding material rather than disappearing after its original release. B.C. Bud Depot’s continued preservation of Blue Buddha in its historical seed catalogs and its use in Purple Buddha document the cultivar’s place within the company’s older genetic library.
Effects and Experience

Blue Buddha rarely begins as heavily as its indica percentage suggests. The first phase can feel cheerful, clear, and mentally open, with a noticeable lift in mood that may encourage conversation, music, or quiet creative activities. Rather than racing forward with Haze -like stimulation, the cerebral side has a softer quality. Thoughts may feel more interesting without becoming difficult to control, and the early portion of the experience can remain surprisingly functional for experienced cannabis consumers.

The shift toward the body happens gradually. What begins as mental ease becomes relaxation through the shoulders, back, and limbs, and physical motivation tends to decrease as the session progresses. Eventually, the heavier side of the hybrid becomes difficult to ignore. Larger doses can produce a deep stone and considerable couch-lock while still leaving a degree of mental awareness intact. That contrast—clear enough to think, heavy enough not to want to move—is one of the cultivar’s most recognizable characteristics.

Historical THC estimates commonly place the strain somewhere from the mid-teens into the low 20% range. Those figures may seem modest beside contemporary marijuana advertised at 30% or more, but Blue Buddha should not automatically be considered weak. THC percentage is only one factor influencing the subjective experience, and mature, terpene-rich flower can feel substantially stronger than its laboratory number implies. Dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, or excessive sedation become more likely when the dose exceeds personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers may find the changing nature of the high particularly useful. The brighter opening can appeal to people who want temporary mental distance from everyday stress without immediately feeling sedated, while the later body effects may become more attractive when physical tension or difficulty settling down is the larger concern. For this reason, Blue Buddha tends to fit late-afternoon or evening use better than situations requiring sustained physical energy.

Its heavier second half may also appeal to cannabis consumers who prefer cultivars that gradually transition toward rest rather than producing immediate drowsiness. Appetite changes, bodily calm, and a quieter mental state may accompany stronger doses, although individual reactions can differ considerably.

Blue Buddha should not be presented as a clinically proven treatment for stress, insomnia, pain, attention disorders, or any other condition. Older marijuana strain descriptions often made broad medical claims that were not supported by controlled clinical trials. Modern medical use is better guided by the actual cannabinoid and terpene analysis of the specific flower, dose, personal tolerance, medications, and advice from an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Blueberry sits at the center of the profile, but the aroma is noticeably more savory than many newer berry strains. Fresh buds can release ripe blueberry, dark fruit, and creamy sweetness followed by cracked pepper and earthy herbs. A faint tea-like character can appear underneath, especially in well-cured flower, giving the cultivar an almost botanical quality. B.C. Bud Depot’s description of Purple Buddha specifically credits Blue Buddha with contributing creamy blueberry flavor to that later hybrid.

Pepper and spice become stronger when the flower is broken apart. Beta-caryophyllene is strongly associated with that character, while limonene can contribute brightness and humulene reinforces the earthy, woody side. Depending on cultivation and phenotype, myrcene may deepen the berry and soil-like qualities while pinene introduces a sharper herbal edge. Exact terpene percentages are not standardized for this older cultivar, so batch testing is more useful than assigning one permanent chemical ratio.

The smoke generally starts sweet. Blueberry and mild cream lead the inhale, followed by herbal tea and fruit through the middle. Earth, pepper, spice, and a subtle diesel quality remain after the exhale. That progression gives Blue Buddha the kind of layered flavor associated with pre-dessert-era marijuana: fruit is important, but it exists alongside soil, herbs, resin, and spice rather than dominating everything else.
Growing Information

Blue Buddha was released as a photoperiod cultivar suitable for both indoor and outdoor cultivation. Historical B.C. Bud Depot specifications place flowering at approximately eight to nine weeks indoors, with outdoor maturity occurring toward late October. The plant was described as producing dense, heavy flowers with significant crystal production, characteristics that made good airflow increasingly important as harvest approached.

Its indica dominance generally keeps the plant more manageable than highly stretchy sativa cannabis, although some phenotypes can still benefit from training. Topping during vegetative growth encourages several productive branches, while low-stress training can widen the canopy and improve light distribution. Dense interior growth should be thinned selectively rather than stripped excessively, particularly once flowering begins.

Yield is better described as moderate to high than attached to an unsupported universal gram figure. Environmental conditions, phenotype, lighting, root volume, vegetative duration, and nutrition all influence production. Outdoors, the late-October finishing time favors regions where autumn remains reasonably dry. Growers in wetter climates should watch dense flowers carefully for moisture problems as maturity approaches. Blue and purple coloration may become more prominent under suitable conditions, but healthy plant development should always take priority over deliberately exposing cannabis to damaging cold merely to intensify color.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Blue Buddha?

Blue Buddha is Oregon Blueberry × Buddha’s Sister. The cultivar became closely associated with B.C. Bud Depot and was later used by the breeder as a parent in Purple Buddha. Historical breeding records also connect the original Blue Buddha work with Moonshineman and Direwulfe.
Is Blue Buddha indica or sativa?

Blue Buddha is an indica-dominant hybrid, commonly described as approximately 75% indica and 25% sativa. Its experience begins more cerebrally than that ratio might suggest before developing into a substantially heavier physical stone.
How strong is Blue Buddha?

Older and modern descriptions commonly place THC somewhere from the mid-teens into the low 20% range. Potency varies by phenotype and cultivation, so laboratory testing of the particular flower is more useful than assuming one fixed percentage.
What does Blue Buddha taste like?
Expect blueberry, dark berries, creamy fruit, herbal tea, pepper, earth, spice, and subtle diesel. The berry character is pronounced but generally less candy-like than modern fruit strains.
How long does Blue Buddha take to flower?

Historical breeder specifications place indoor flowering at roughly eight to nine weeks. Outdoors, the original B.C. Bud Depot material was expected to finish around late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Blue Buddha

Blue Buddha captures a style of cannabis breeding that has become increasingly rare. Oregon Blueberry provides fruit, color, and deep relaxation, while Buddha’s Sister adds enough spice, herbs, cerebral activity, and resin to keep the cultivar from behaving like a conventional blueberry indica. The resulting flower can smell sweet and inviting without losing the peppery earth and diesel character that gives older weed strains much of their personality.

Its legacy is also visible in subsequent breeding. B.C. Bud Depot preserved Blue Buddha in its catalog and used it directly to create Purple Buddha, combining its creamy blueberry character with The Purps. An eight-to-nine-week indoor flowering period, dense resinous flowers, distinctive berry-and-spice terpenes, and a high that progresses from mental uplift into serious body relaxation make the cultivar more than a historical curiosity. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in blueberry genetics from before the modern dominance of Gelato, Cookies, and Runtz, Blue Buddha offers a flavorful connection to an earlier period of North American marijuana breeding.
